candidates.citation: NV CR 25-16 (Carson City — Lake Tahoe and tributaries)

parameters.note: North Canyon Creek is a west-slope Carson Range stream that drains toward Lake Tahoe (OSM way 543128054; mouth near 39.10005, -119.94674), so it is a Lake Tahoe tributary. NDOW classifies it under Carson City County (Western Region), and it is governed by the Carson City 'Lake Tahoe and tributaries' listing in CR 25-16: open year-round, with restricted hours and a 5/10 game-fish limit. This specific sub-listing overrides the Carson City general 'All waters' default (5 trout, 5 mountain whitefish, and 15 warmwater game fish daily; any hour). Carson City has no closed waters in CR 25-16, so no part of this creek is closed — unlike the Washoe County side of Lake Tahoe, where Third, Incline, and Wood creeks are closed. This is the Nevada rule; it differs from the California §7.50(b)(152) seasonal catch-and-release closure that applies to Tahoe tributaries on the California side of the lake. County note: NDOW's waters database lists this creek as Carson City; its lower reach lies close to the Carson City–Douglas County line (OSM/Nominatim places the representative point near the boundary), but Douglas County's CR 25-16 'Lake Tahoe and tributaries' listing is identical to Carson City's, so nothing turns on the exact line.

candidates.summary: Open year-round as a Lake Tahoe tributary (Carson City 'Lake Tahoe and tributaries' listing); Carson City lists no closed waters.

parameters.counting_rule: The Carson City 'Lake Tahoe and tributaries' listing sets 5 game fish daily and 10 in possession, with no species sub-limit. 'Game fish' in Nevada includes trout, mountain whitefish, kokanee salmon, bass, and other listed game species combined.

candidates.summary: 5 game fish daily, 10 in possession (Lake Tahoe and tributaries listing; no species sub-limit).

candidates.citation: NV CR 25-16 (Carson City — Lake Tahoe and tributaries)

parameters.note: The Carson City 'Lake Tahoe and tributaries' listing restricts fishing hours to 1 hour before sunrise through 2 hours after sunset (unlike Carson City's general 'All waters' default, which allows fishing any hour of the day or night).

candidates.summary: Fishing hours: 1 hour before sunrise to 2 hours after sunset.

parameters.note: Nevada requires a fishing license for residents and nonresidents 12 years of age or older; anglers under 12 need no license (nonresidents under 12 are limited to 50% of the daily bag). The California/Nevada Lake Tahoe license reciprocity (and the Nevada Interstate Boundary Waters License) applies to fishing IN Lake Tahoe itself, not to its tributaries above the lake — a Nevada fishing license is required to fish North Canyon Creek.

candidates.summary: Nevada fishing license required for anglers 12+ (Lake Tahoe license reciprocity does not extend to the tributary).
